overview.title: See the adjustment
overview.lead: In TPLO simulation, the radiograph remains the reference for visualizing the defined fragment and following its rotation. Enter the angle, observe the resulting position and review the construction of the plan in the context of the case.
overview.fragment: Define the fragment from the cut geometry. The original outline remains a reference for following the selected region and understanding what is being moved on the image.
overview.rotation: The entered rotation is applied to the selected fragment. The original and resulting outlines show the change in position while preserving the references used to construct the plan.
overview.review: Review the result on the radiograph and save the simulation in the plan. When you return to the case, the recorded cut, fragment and parameters remain available for reference.

setup.question: What do I need to define before simulating?
setup.answer: In TPLO simulation, define the cut geometry, including its center and radius, and outline the fragment that will move. These references let you visualize the selected region on the radiograph.

rotation.question: How is rotation applied to the fragment?
rotation.answer: You enter the rotation angle and follow the selected fragment's change in position on the image. The preview lets you review the adjustment alongside the planning references.

reference.question: Can I compare the original position with the result?
reference.answer: Yes. The original outline remains a reference while the fragment moves. This lets you observe the difference between the positions and review the simulation on the radiograph itself.

saved.question: Are the parameters available after saving?
saved.answer: Yes. When you save the simulation in the plan, the recorded cut, fragment and parameters remain linked to the plan for reference when you return to the case.
